/-!
# Crouzeix's conjecture

Crouzeix's conjecture (M. Crouzeix, 2004) states that for every $n \times n$ complex matrix $A$
and every complex function $f$ that is analytic in the interior of the field of values
(numerical range) $W(A) = \{x^* A x : \|x\| = 1\}$ of $A$ and continuous up to its boundary,
$$\|f(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm. Equivalently, the inequality holds for
every complex polynomial $p$ in place of $f$.

Crouzeix proved the inequality with the constant $11.08$ in place of $2$ (2007), and Crouzeix and
Palencia improved the constant to $1 + \sqrt 2$ (2017). Proofs of the conjecture were announced
in 2026 (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Crouzeix's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crouzeix%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- M. Crouzeix, *Bounds for analytical functions of matrices*, Integral Equations and Operator
  Theory 48 (2004), 461–477. [doi:10.1007/s00020-002-1188-6](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00020-002-1188-6)
- M. Crouzeix, *Numerical range and functional calculus in Hilbert space*, Journal of Functional
  Analysis 244 (2007), 668–690. [doi:10.1016/j.jfa.2006.10.013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfa.2006.10.013)
- M. Crouzeix, C. Palencia, *The numerical range is a $(1+\sqrt2)$-spectral set*, SIAM Journal on
  Matrix Analysis and Applications 38 (2017), 649–655.
  [doi:10.1137/17M1116672](https://doi.org/10.1137/17M1116672)
- E. Lorist, F. Schwenninger, *A solution to Crouzeix's conjecture*,
  [arXiv:2608.03841](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03841)
-/

def numericalRange (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z | ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪x, toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ = z}
blocks.docstring:
The **field of values** (or **numerical range**) $W(A) = \{x^* A x : \|x\| = 1\}$ of a square
complex matrix `A`, where `x` ranges over the unit vectors of `EuclideanSpace ℂ n`. Here
`⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ = x^* A x` because Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in its first
argument.

justification.closest_existing_considered: spectrum ℂ A (too small: only eigenvalues), Matrix.toEuclideanCLM / Matrix.toEuclideanLin (used to build the definition), ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient (real-valued, self-adjoint setting only).
justification.name: CrouzeixsConjecture.numericalRange
justification.why_needed: The numerical range / field of values W(A) = {⟨x, Ax⟩ : ‖x‖ = 1} is not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (grep for numericalRange / 'numerical range' / 'field of values' returns nothing). Defined as {z | ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪x, toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ = z}; Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first argument so this is x* A x. Three API tests (zero, one, diagonal) included.

@[category API, AMS 15 47]
theorem isCompact_numericalRange (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : IsCompact (numericalRange A) := by
  have : numericalRange A =
      (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n => ⟪x, toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ) '' Metric.sphere 0 1 := by
    ext z
    simp [numericalRange]
  rw [this]
  exact (isCompact_sphere 0 1).image <|
    continuous_id.inner (toEuclideanLin A).continuous_of_finiteDimensional

def IsFunctionalCalculus (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ → ℂ[X],
    TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k z => (p k).eval z) f atTop (numericalRange A) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k => aeval A (p k)) atTop (𝓝 B)
blocks.docstring:
`IsFunctionalCalculus A f B` says that `B = f(A)`, where `f(A)` is the continuous extension
(Delyon–Delyon, Crouzeix) of the polynomial functional calculus `p ↦ p(A)` to the functions `f`
that are continuous on the numerical range `W(A)` and analytic in its interior: `B` is the limit
of `p k (A)` for a sequence of polynomials `p k` converging uniformly to `f` on `W(A)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Polynomial.aeval (only polynomials; used inside the definition), cfc / continuous functional calculus (requires IsStarNormal), NormedSpace.exp / analytic functional calculus via power series (requires entire functions or convergence on a disc).
justification.name: CrouzeixsConjecture.IsFunctionalCalculus
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no functional calculus f ↦ f(A) for non-normal matrices and functions merely analytic in the interior of W(A) and continuous on W(A) (the continuous functional calculus needs normality, the Riesz–Dunford/holomorphic calculus needs analyticity on a neighbourhood of the spectrum, which may lie on ∂W(A)). IsFunctionalCalculus A f B says B is the limit of p k (A) for a sequence of polynomials p k converging uniformly to f on W(A), i.e. B = f(A) for the Delyon–Delyon/Crouzeix continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus from the (Mergelyan-dense) polynomials to A(W(A)). Well-definedness (independence of the sequence) is Crouzeix's 11.08 theorem; existence of an approximating sequence is Mergelyan's theorem; the conjecture is quantified over all such B so it does not rely on either. API test: IsFunctionalCalculus A p.eval (aeval A p).

/-- `IsFunctionalCalculus A f B` says that `B = f(A)`, where `f(A)` is the continuous extension
(Delyon–Delyon, Crouzeix) of the polynomial functional calculus `p ↦ p(A)` to the functions `f`
that are continuous on the numerical range `W(A)` and analytic in its interior: `B` is the limit
of `p k (A)` for a sequence of polynomials `p k` converging uniformly to `f` on `W(A)`. -/
def IsFunctionalCalculus (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ → ℂ[X],
    TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k z => (p k).eval z) f atTop (numericalRange A) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k => aeval A (p k)) atTop (𝓝 B)

theorem isFunctionalCalculus_aeval (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (p : ℂ[X]) :

theorem crouzeixs_conjecture [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A))
    (hf' : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A)))
    (B : Matrix n n ℂ) (hB : IsFunctionalCalculus A f B) :
    ‖B‖ ≤ 2 * sSup ((fun z => ‖f z‖) '' numericalRange A) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Crouzeix's conjecture.** Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ complex matrix ($n \geq 1$) and let $f$ be
a complex function that is analytic in the interior of the field of values (numerical range)
$W(A) = \{x^* A x : \|x\| = 1\}$ of $A$ and continuous up to its boundary. Then
$$\|f(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm (`Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`) and $f(A)$ is
given by the continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus (`IsFunctionalCalculus`).

claims.decomposer_note: Implicit universal quantifiers over every n ≥ 1, every A ∈ M_n(ℂ) and every f continuous on the (compact, convex) numerical range W(A) = {⟨Ax,x⟩ : ‖x‖ = 1} and analytic on its interior (which may be empty, e.g. for normal A with collinear spectrum, making the analyticity hypothesis vacuous); the norm is the spectral operator 2-norm, the bound is non-strict with constant exactly 2 (sharp already for the 2×2 nilpotent Jordan block), and f(A) is the (Delyon–Delyon/Crouzeix) continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus to A(W(A)) — Mathlib has no numerical-range definition, so W(A) must be defined; the article reports 2026 claimed proofs (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger) but the problem is listed here as open.
claims.reviewer_why: c04's relational ∀-form is used: for every B with IsFunctionalCalculus A f B (B = lim p_k(A) for polynomials p_k → f uniformly on W(A), i.e. the Delyon–Delyon/Crouzeix continuous extension of the polynomial calculus), ‖B‖ ≤ 2·sup_{W(A)}|f|, with f ContinuousOn W(A) and AnalyticOnNhd on interior W(A) (vacuous when the interior is empty, as intended), spectral norm via scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator (verified to elaborate to Matrix.instL2OpNormedRing), W(A) = {⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ : ‖x‖ = 1} = {x*Ax} (conjugation convention verified; 1×1 test included). This form is unconditionally equivalent to the polynomial form (constant sequence ⇒; limit ⇐) and introduces no junk values, unlike c08's limUnder (junk if the limit does not exist) or the ∃-forms of c02/c03/c05/c07 (which add an existence claim and rely on uniqueness of B via Crouzeix 2007 to be equivalent to the conjecture). Edits: added [Nonempty n] (n ≥ 1 per source, guarantees W(A) ≠ ∅ so the sup is genuine), used sSup of the image of ‖f‖ over W(A) (c06 style) instead of ⨆; added compactness API lemma (c01/c06) and the 1×1 conjugation test (c08).
claims.source_text: the matrix norm of a complex function $f$ applied to a complex matrix $A$ is at most twice the supremum of $|f(z)|$ over the field of values of $A$
claims.text_span: the matrix norm of a complex function $f$ applied to a complex matrix $A$ is at most twice the supremum of $|f(z)|$ over the field of values of $A$

claims.decomposer_note: Equivalent reformulation (the form used in Crouzeix 2004 and all cited papers): for all n ≥ 1, all A ∈ M_n(ℂ) and all p ∈ ℂ[X], ‖p(A)‖₂ ≤ 2 · sup_{z ∈ W(A)} |p(z)| with p(A) = Polynomial.aeval A p; equivalent to the analytic form by density of polynomials in A(W(A)) (Mergelyan/Delyon–Delyon), and avoids defining a functional calculus for non-polynomial f.
claims.reviewer_why: ‖aeval A p‖ ≤ 2 * sSup ((fun z => ‖p.eval z‖) '' numericalRange A) for every A : Matrix n n ℂ with n a nonempty finite type and every p : ℂ[X], spectral norm via the scoped L2 operator instance. All candidates agree on this slot up to the sup spelling and the n ≥ 1 encoding; c04's declaration was used with [Nonempty n] added and sSup-of-image spelling. W(A) is compact and nonempty and p is continuous, so the sSup is the true supremum.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Crouzeix's conjecture

Crouzeix's conjecture (M. Crouzeix, 2004) states that for every $n \times n$ complex matrix $A$
and every complex function $f$ that is analytic in the interior of the field of values
(numerical range) $W(A) = \{x^* A x : \|x\| = 1\}$ of $A$ and continuous up to its boundary,
$$\|f(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm. Equivalently, the inequality holds for
every complex polynomial $p$ in place of $f$.

Crouzeix proved the inequality with the constant $11.08$ in place of $2$ (2007), and Crouzeix and
Palencia improved the constant to $1 + \sqrt 2$ (2017). Proofs of the conjecture were announced
in 2026 (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Crouzeix's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crouzeix%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- M. Crouzeix, *Bounds for analytical functions of matrices*, Integral Equations and Operator
  Theory 48 (2004), 461–477. [doi:10.1007/s00020-002-1188-6](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00020-002-1188-6)
- M. Crouzeix, *Numerical range and functional calculus in Hilbert space*, Journal of Functional
  Analysis 244 (2007), 668–690. [doi:10.1016/j.jfa.2006.10.013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfa.2006.10.013)
- M. Crouzeix, C. Palencia, *The numerical range is a $(1+\sqrt2)$-spectral set*, SIAM Journal on
  Matrix Analysis and Applications 38 (2017), 649–655.
  [doi:10.1137/17M1116672](https://doi.org/10.1137/17M1116672)
- E. Lorist, F. Schwenninger, *A solution to Crouzeix's conjecture*,
  [arXiv:2608.03841](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03841)
-/

open Filter Matrix Polynomial Topology
open scoped InnerProductSpace Matrix.Norms.L2Operator

namespace CrouzeixsConjecture

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- The **field of values** (or **numerical range**) $W(A) = \{x^* A x : \|x\| = 1\}$ of a square
complex matrix `A`, where `x` ranges over the unit vectors of `EuclideanSpace ℂ n`. Here
`⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ = x^* A x` because Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in its first
argument. -/
def numericalRange (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z | ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪x, toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ = z}

/-- The numerical range of a matrix is compact. -/
@[category API, AMS 15 47]
theorem isCompact_numericalRange (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : IsCompact (numericalRange A) := by
  have : numericalRange A =
      (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n => ⟪x, toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ) '' Metric.sphere 0 1 := by
    ext z
    simp [numericalRange]
  rw [this]
  exact (isCompact_sphere 0 1).image <|
    continuous_id.inner (toEuclideanLin A).continuous_of_finiteDimensional

@[category test, AMS 15 47]
theorem mem_numericalRange_diagonal (d : n → ℂ) (i : n) : d i ∈ numericalRange (diagonal d) :=
  ⟨EuclideanSpace.single i 1, by simp,
    by simp [toEuclideanLin_apply, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left]⟩

@[category test, AMS 15 47]
theorem numericalRange_one [Nonempty n] : numericalRange (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) = {1} := by
  ext z
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    simp only [toEuclideanLin_apply, one_mulVec, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    rw [WithLp.toLp_ofLp, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, hx]
    simp
  · rintro rfl
    exact mem_numericalRange_diagonal (fun _ => 1) (Classical.arbitrary n)

/-- The numerical range of the `1 × 1` matrix `(a)` is `{a}` (and not `{conj a}`). -/
@[category test, AMS 15 47]
theorem numericalRange_fin_one (a : ℂ) : numericalRange !![a] = {a} := by
  have h : toEuclideanLin !![a] = a • LinearMap.id :=
    LinearMap.ext fun v => by ext i; fin_cases i; simp [toEuclideanLin_apply, vecHead]
  ext w
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    simp [h, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, hx]
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨EuclideanSpace.single 0 1, by simp, by simp [h, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]⟩

/-- `IsFunctionalCalculus A f B` says that `B = f(A)`, where `f(A)` is the continuous extension
(Delyon–Delyon, Crouzeix) of the polynomial functional calculus `p ↦ p(A)` to the functions `f`
that are continuous on the numerical range `W(A)` and analytic in its interior: `B` is the limit
of `p k (A)` for a sequence of polynomials `p k` converging uniformly to `f` on `W(A)`. -/
def IsFunctionalCalculus (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ → ℂ[X],
    TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k z => (p k).eval z) f atTop (numericalRange A) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k => aeval A (p k)) atTop (𝓝 B)

/-- For a polynomial `p`, `p(A)` is the usual polynomial evaluation `aeval A p`. -/
@[category test, AMS 15 47]
theorem isFunctionalCalculus_aeval (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    IsFunctionalCalculus A (fun z => p.eval z) (aeval A p) :=
  ⟨fun _ => p, fun _ hu => Eventually.of_forall fun _ _ _ => refl_mem_uniformity hu,
    tendsto_const_nhds⟩

/--
**Crouzeix's conjecture.** Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ complex matrix ($n \geq 1$) and let $f$ be
a complex function that is analytic in the interior of the field of values (numerical range)
$W(A) = \{x^* A x : \|x\| = 1\}$ of $A$ and continuous up to its boundary. Then
$$\|f(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm (`Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`) and $f(A)$ is
given by the continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus (`IsFunctionalCalculus`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A))
    (hf' : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A)))
    (B : Matrix n n ℂ) (hB : IsFunctionalCalculus A f B) :
    ‖B‖ ≤ 2 * sSup ((fun z => ‖f z‖) '' numericalRange A) := by
  sorry

/--
**Crouzeix's conjecture, polynomial form.** For every $n \times n$ complex matrix $A$
($n \geq 1$) and every complex polynomial $p$,
$$\|p(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |p(z)|,$$
where $W(A)$ is the field of values (numerical range) of $A$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral
operator $2$-norm (`Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture.variants.polynomial [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    ‖aeval A p‖ ≤ 2 * sSup ((fun z => ‖p.eval z‖) '' numericalRange A) := by
  sorry

end CrouzeixsConjecture

items: The list-page statement is terse; the precise formulation (f analytic in the interior of W(A) and continuous up to its boundary; norm = spectral operator 2-norm; polynomial reformulation) was taken from the Wikipedia article and Crouzeix 2004 / Lorist–Schwenninger 2026, exactly as the decomposition notes prescribe.

Matrix size is modelled as an arbitrary finite index type n with [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (repo idiom) rather than Fin n with n ≥ 1. No [Nonempty n] hypothesis: for empty n, W(A) = ∅, the sup is 0 and ‖B‖ = 0, so the inequality holds trivially and the statement is not weakened.
The norm is Mathlib's scoped L2 operator norm instance (open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator); checked with pp.explicit that ‖·‖ elaborates to Matrix.instL2OpNormedRing, i.e. the spectral 2-norm.

The supremum is written ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖f z‖ in ℝ. Since W(A) is compact and f is continuous on it (hypothesis hf, and in the polynomial case automatically), the set is bounded and the real iSup is the genuine supremum; for empty W(A) it is 0.

'Analytic in the interior' is AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A)); on an open subset of ℂ this coincides with DifferentiableOn ℂ. When the interior is empty (normal A with collinear spectrum) the hypothesis is vacuous, as in the source.

f(A) is modelled relationally (IsFunctionalCalculus A f B) rather than as a function, to avoid a Classical.choose/limUnder definition; the theorem quantifies over every B in the relation. The hypotheses hf, hf' are mathematically implied by IsFunctionalCalculus (uniform limits of polynomials are continuous and analytic inside) but are kept so the Lean statement mirrors the source wording.
Category research open, as instructed, even though the article reports 2026 claimed proofs (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger). AMS 15 (matrix theory) and 47 (operator theory).
The ⟨Ax,x⟩ convention of Lorist–Schwenninger (linear in the first variable) and Mathlib's ⟪x, Ax⟫ (conjugate-linear in the first variable) both equal x* A x, so the numerical range is the same set.

reviewer_notes: Both slots ship. Source statement is terse; hypotheses on f (continuous on W(A), analytic in its interior), the spectral 2-norm, and the polynomial reformulation were taken from the dedicated Wikipedia article as the decomposition notes prescribe. Key decisions: (1) f(A) is encoded relationally (IsFunctionalCalculus) and universally quantified — the statement is then exactly equivalent to the polynomial form without appeal to Mergelyan or Crouzeix's 11.08 bound, and there is no junk-valued term; the hypotheses hf, hf' are mathematically implied by IsFunctionalCalculus but kept so the Lean mirrors the source wording. (2) Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first argument, so ⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ = x*Ax, the standard field of values; verified by test numericalRange_fin_one (W([a]) = {a}, not {conj a}) — using ⟪A x, x⟫ would have given the conjugate set and changed sup|p|. (3) [Nonempty n] encodes n ≥ 1; the excluded n = 0 case is trivially 0 ≤ 0, so this is harmless and matches the source. (4) Category research open per the given status although the article reports 2026 announced proofs (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger); these are mentioned in the module docstring. Omitted from c01: extra research-solved variants (normal matrices, Crouzeix–Palencia bound) since they are not adjudicated slots. All candidates' omission lists were empty; no decomposition objections of substance.
